newsitem.title: Sudanese rebels say they capture Warab town.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese rebels say they capture Warab town.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Wednesday they had taken the southern town of Warab.

Yassir Arman, spokesman in the Eritrean capital Asmara for the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), said: "The SPLA forces yesterday at 5.30 p.m. local time (1530 GMT) captured Warab town, which is the capital of Warabi state."

Warab is 1,000 km (600 miles) south of the capital Khartoum and just north of Tonj, a town the SPLA says it captured last Friday. Arman said it was the hometown of the Sudanese Vice President, Police Major-General George Kongor Arop.
The spokesman said that in Tonj last week the rebels captured 56 trucks in good condition and took prisoner the governor of Buheyrat state, Ramsay Montong.
The rebels, in coordination with northern opposition groups operating in the northeast, launched their current offensive in January. They have seized a string of towns in the south.
